title: What do Christmas market traders say about rising prices?

input.lead: From £8 bratwursts to £11 Yorkshire pudding wraps, why is the cost of the markets rising year on year?
input.summary: From £8 bratwursts to £11 Yorkshire pudding wraps, why is the cost of the markets rising year on year?
input.evidence_text: Mention Christmas markets these days and the conversation often turns to rising prices – from £8 bratwursts, £11 Yorkshire pudding wraps and even £5 for a few marshmallow sticks But what do the people behind the stalls think? Are they benefiting from the hikes or are their own profits being squeezed? Traders at Manchester's Christmas markets told the BBC they were feeling the pressure of increasing bills for staff, ingredients and energy, with some saying they were making less money despite charging more One trader said it costs at least £4,000 a day to run each her four stalls, while another has cut prices to keep customers coming back Nils Borstel, 25, helps run Bratwurst King, a family business which has operated at the markets since 1999 He said a sausage that previously cost £3.50 now sold for £8, with much of the increase taking place over the past five or six years

title: Conservative Party pays artist for Burnham images after legal threat

input.lead: Stanley Chow had threatened to sue the Conservative Party for using his illustrations of the PM
input.summary: Stanley Chow had threatened to sue the Conservative Party for using his illustrations of the PM
input.evidence_text: The Conservatives have agreed to pay an artist who threatened to sue the party after it used his illustration of Andy Burnham to mock the prime minister Stanley Chow posted on Facebook that the party had used the picture - which Burnham has used on social media - without permission He had sought legal advice and threatened to take action against the party. It is understood the Tories agreed to pay a £1,000 fee for use of the image - and contributed an unknown sum to Chow's legal fees The Conservatives had distributed water bottles with the image on them - accusing Burnham of being a "bottler" Chow posted on Facebook: "The Conservative Party have settled after their recent indiscretion of using my image without my permission." He added: "Maybe ask first… admittedly I would have said no, but it would have been a damn sight cheaper for the Tory Party if they just hired any illustrator to do their take on a cartoon of Burnham… hopefully this a lesson learned. Copyright matters."

title: Dismay as Leigh veterans' handmade war memorial stolen

input.lead: Handmade wooden silhouettes of soldiers have been taken from a roundabout in Leigh
input.summary: Handmade wooden silhouettes of soldiers have been taken from a roundabout in Leigh
input.evidence_text: Dismay as Leigh veterans' handmade war memorial stolen - BBC News Image source, Reeva Programme Image caption, The soldiers represent members of the armed forces who have died in conflicts since 1914 By Emma Jackson and Richard Stead , North West Published 13 November 2026 Veterans who handmade memorials to fallen soldiers were dismayed to find they had been stolen. They discovered that four of the wooden silhouettes had been taken from the display near Leigh Sports Village in in Greater Manchester was made earlier by members of a group set up to support ex-service people. George Brooks, who launched The Reeva Programme, said: "We are absolutely gutted. "I'm upset, I'm angry, and I'm sad, because I know the effort that went into making every single one of those crosses, making every single one of those tommies." Image source, Reeva Programme Image caption, George Brooks founded The Reeva Programme CIC. The memorial, created on a roundabout, also features 1,228 white crosses to represent local members of the armed forces who were killed in World War Two and subsequent conflicts. George, 35, who served with the Army in Afghanistan, said the stolen figures were important to the community, and to thousands of people they were not just "pieces of wood". Image source, Reeva Programme Image caption, Reeva is named after a therapy dog that helped Brooks cope with PTSD after he left the Army The Reeva Programme provides fully trained assistance dogs to those who have served in the armed forces or emergency services. The theft has been reported to the police, but Brooks posted on social media to say that if whoever had stolen them were to return them, that would be the end of it. title: Manchester Our Pass bus scheme to give free travel for 11-16s

input.lead: Extra enforcement officers are being recruited ahead of 11-16 year olds being able to ride buses in the city for free from January
input.summary: Extra enforcement officers are being recruited ahead of 11-16 year olds being able to ride buses in the city for free from January
input.evidence_text: The Mayor of Greater Manchester has said the city region's combined authority is "preparing" for anti-social behaviour ahead of the roll-out of free bus travel for 11 to 16-year-olds From January, the current Our Pass scheme, which gives 16- 18-year-olds free travel on the Bee Network, will be extended to children from the age of 11 Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) confirmed that it was recruiting 20 extra travel safe and enforcement officers to support the 121 existing roles which coincided with the roll-out The city region's Mayor, Bev Craig said the combined authority had been working to make the Bee Network "even safer", and that "we trust our young people." Recent measures included the recent creation of the Transport Policing and Crime Command, which has seen 60 new police officers patrolling Manchester's trams and buses She said the new scheme for 11 to 16-year-olds, expected to benefit 200,000 young people, builds on the Our Pass scheme allowing free bus travel to those aged 16 to 18 which was rolled out in 2019

input.evidence_text: A global Microsoft outage has been disrupting most workplaces and services across the north-west of England NHS, police and fire services, along with schools, have warned people about emails being down and finding work-around ways to help keep in contact. title: Handmade gates craned into place at Rochdale Canal lock in Manchester

input.lead: The new gates at Rochdale Canal lock in Manchester replace ones installed more than 25 years ago
input.summary: The new gates at Rochdale Canal lock in Manchester replace ones installed more than 25 years ago
input.evidence_text: Work has begun to restore lock gates across Greater Manchester's historical canal network A team has started fitting new handmade gates at Lock 80 on the Rochdale Canal, a waterway opened in 1804 as the first of three trans-Pennine canals, running between Manchester and Sowerby Bridge, West Yorkshire The new gates, at the lock to the east of the city centre in Manchester, were handcrafted from oak in Yorkshire, before being craned into place Each leaf of the upstream gate weighs one-and-a-half tonnes (1,500 kg), and the downstream leaves weigh two-and-a-half tonnes (2,500 kg). They replace gates that were installed at the turn of the millennium It comes after canal gates were replaced in the stretch of canal running through Manchester's Gay Village, in February The Canal and River Trust, the charity that cares for canals and waterways across England and Wales, said the work was one of hundreds of projects over the next five months set to maintain the 2,000-mile canal network

input.evidence_text: The Mayor of Greater Manchester, Bev Craig OBE, has called for the city region’s economic growth to put more wealth and opportunity in the hands of local communities, naming co-operatives, social enterprises and community ownership as central to making that happen Craig was speaking at Thrive Together: GM Social Enterprise Summit at New Century Hall, Manchester. The summit was held alongside the National Social Enterprise Summit, ahead of this evening’s (Thursday 12 November) UK Social Enterprise Awards A growing economy does not automatically make life better, Craig said, contrasting Greater Manchester’s visible development with neighbourhoods where residents still struggle financially, and where high streets have lost shops, services and investment The Mayor said: “Good growth is about keeping the benefits of growth in the pockets of the people who create it. A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. input.evidence_text: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. The plan sets out an ambition to create 200,000 entry-level jobs, including apprenticeships, during that period The plan also addresses how AI is changing workforce requirements and the importance of ensuring people entering the industry have both technical knowledge and practical workplace skills Manchester Digital's 2026 Sector Insights Report highlighted a reduction of around 20% in early-career opportunities, despite continued demand for experienced technology professionals
